title: The search lexer strips commas even inside quotes, so no comma-bearing label value (including #geolocation) can be matched by equality
statement: The search lexer treats ',' as an operator character and, after the quoted-string branch has closed, discards every comma it sees regardless of lexer state, quoted or not. A label value like the documented #geolocation="48.8583,2.2945" is therefore lexed as 48.85832.2945 and matches nothing that was ever stored, in every quoting form including the double-quoted one the Geo Map manual explicitly instructs the user to type. The query answers HTTP 200 with an empty list, with no error and no warning. A backslash-escaped comma does match, but escaping is not mentioned anywhere in the geo-map or search documentation.

handVerified.note: Report section 5. Stored value read back first as ["48.8583,2.2945"] to rule out a write problem; all three quoting forms answered 200 []. Controls: label-existence returns the note, an identically shaped quoted equality on a comma-free value matches, and the contains operator *=* reaches the note. The escape hatch #geolocation="48.8583\,2.2945" was verified to match. The report also corrects findings.md: its *= probe was mislabelled, *= is ends-with, so its empty answer there was correct and not a comma effect; the conclusion is unaffected.

source.howDecided: No commit touches lex.ts between the tested commit and head; the blob is identical at tested, head and v0.105.0. Re-read at head: line 16 still declares ',' an operator character in isSymbolAnOperator, the `} else if (!quotes) {` branch still opens at :91 and closes at :123, and :125-127 `if (chr === ",") { continue; }` still sits after that close, so it runs in every lexer state including inside quotes. Open PR #10633 does patch lex.ts, but with a single hunk at :93-105 that adds two-character fuzzy-operator handling; it does not touch the comma line, so that PR does not fix this.

queries: gh search issues --repo TriliumNext/Trilium 'comma search attribute value'

reevaluation: Stands and remains unreported; both searches returned nothing and the recency sweep of every issue created since 2026-08-01 contains nothing related. Source is unchanged and shipped in v0.105.0. The impact is broader than the geo map: any label whose value contains a comma is unreachable by equality, and the Geo Map page (:72-74 and :157) is the documentation that tells users to store precisely such a value and to wrap it in quotes, so the manual walks the user into the failure. Confidence is high because the mechanism is a single unconditional `continue` three lines below the close of the unquoted branch, and because the escaped form matching proves the rest of the pipeline is sound.
notes: Lead with the geo-map instruction, because it makes the report self-evidently a bug rather than a preference: the manual tells the user to write #geolocation="lat,lon" and that exact value is unsearchable. Do not repeat findings.md's *= probe as evidence; *= is ends-with (build_comparator.ts:46) and its empty answer is correct. Use *=* if a contrast operator is needed. Mention the backslash escape as an undocumented workaround, not as the fix.
